A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WSRL and provide readable main text, equations, figures, and appendices. Existing content can be matched despite the added robot experiment and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original RL experiments on Antmaze, Kitchen, Adroit, and MuJoCo, together with extensive ablations and diagnostic analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the simulation experiments and adds original physical-robot peg-insertion results in Section 5.7 and Table 1.

M1.justification: The WSRL warmup and subsequent SAC procedure remain unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithm 1. The new robot instantiation adds image and proprioceptive inputs, a pre-trained ResNet encoder, and classifier-generated rewards (Section 5.7 and Appendix J), constituting a limited model adaptation.

E1.justification: v3 extends the simulation-only evaluation to physical Franka peg insertion using wrist-camera observations and a newly collected dataset of approximately 17,000 transitions. This introduces a materially different domain and input environment; the existing simulation coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 introduces SERL as an explicitly evaluated robot comparator and includes the offline CalQL checkpoint as a reference. SERL is an RLPD-based robot implementation, so this is a limited comparator extension. Existing simulation comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds a separate physical-robot protocol: asynchronous collection and learning, 10 Hz control, classifier rewards, bounded random resets, 40,000 offline gradient steps, and online runs of 20,000 environment steps. Evaluation uses 20 initial poses and reports elapsed training time. These are new experimental settings, not revisions to the retained simulation protocols.

E4.justification: Section 5.7 and Figure 15 add a qualitative robot case study contrasting successful WSRL insertion with SERL drifting or stalling. The existing warmup, initialization, policy-freezing, retention, normalization, ensemble, and UTD ablations are retained, including their appendix results.

E5.justification: The existing shaded-band reporting practice is retained without new explanations of seed counts or uncertainty estimation. The robot experiment specifies 20 evaluation poses, which is an evaluation sample size; it adds no independent training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New robot results report WSRL achieving 20/20 successes after 18 minutes, versus offline CalQL's 13/20 and SERL's 0/20 after 50 minutes. Figure 6 also revises RLPD curves: its Antmaze-large-play score at 400,000 steps changes from approximately 0.65 to 0.80, and its Door-binary learning trajectory changes. Most existing simulation results are retained.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, optimization objective, and mathematical content of the existing diagnostics remain unchanged. v3 adds no formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: offline-data retention is unnecessary with suitable warmup and online RL, and WSRL mitigates forgetting while enabling efficient fine-tuning. The robot experiment supplies additional support without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.7 adds interpretations of SERL's robot failures and WSRL's effective use of offline initialization. Appendix O adds advice to use alternatives such as online RL when initialization is poor; the underlying failure limitation already appeared in v1 Appendix N. Figure 5 also clarifies that continued conservative regularization is conditional on its presence.

D1.justification: v3 newly provides code-access information for both WSRL and the robot experiments. Appendix J adds substantial reproduction details, including robot hardware and execution, human-assisted data collection, reward-classifier training on 200 positive and 500 negative examples, network architecture, and optimization settings. The earlier simulation implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to SERL, human-in-the-loop robotic RL, and the functional manipulation benchmark to support the robot experiment. The broader research positioning in Section 6 remains substantially unchanged; reference renumbering and the duplicated RLPD reference do not constitute new research relationships.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and typo corrections and inserts Section 5.7 and Appendix J. Existing appendices J–N become K–O, while most prose, terminology, and narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds robot Table 1 and Figures 14–15, adjusts Figure 5's labels and spacing, and relocates several retained appendix plots. The overall layout and existing plot designs remain stable; Figure 6's changed curve values are result changes rather than a display redesign.

improvement.justification: v1 already provided extensive simulation and ablation evidence. v3 adds physical-robot validation absent from v1 and improves reproducibility information through robot implementation details and code-access links. The gain is bounded: the robot evidence covers one task and 20 evaluation poses without reported training-run uncertainty, while the central method and most supporting analyses remain unchanged.
